Rajiv Singh:

first earnings conference call of Karamtara Engineering Limited as a listed company. Our results

At the outset, on behalf of the Karamtara family, I would like to thank every investor who has 
participated in our fundraising journey and placed their trust in us. Our listing on the stock 
exchange is an important milestone in our journey that started almost three decades ago. And 
we see it as the beginning of a long-term relationship with our shareholders. 
 
We have delivered a strong quarterly performance in Q1 FY27 in terms of both revenue and 
profit, making a strong start to our journey as a listed company. Since this is our first interaction 
with many of you, I will like to introduce Karamtara and our ecosystem to you. 
 
Karamtara was incorporated in 1996 and was built on a strong foundation in power transmission, 
with deep expertise in the manufacturing of lattice towers and renewable steel structures. Over 
the years, we continue to strengthen these core capabilities, expand our product portfolio, and 
build scale with establishing ourselves as a trusted partner across the renewable and transmission 
ecosystem globally.

Today, we are very strongly present in all the four major geographies outside of China, namely 
India, U.S., Saudi Arabia, and Europe, with 12 different products in our portfolio. Today, 
Karamtara is a backward-integrated manufacturer of products for the sectors we operate in. 
Currently, we operate 13 manufacturing facilities: eight in Maharashtra, of which seven at Boisar 
and one at Nagpur; four in Gujarat, at Bhachau; and one in Italy. 
 
We, further, have two new facilities coming up at our complex in Bhachau: one new rolling mill 
to support our transmission tower business and solar tracker piles, and one for PEB focused on 
data centers. We also have one solar stamped part facility coming up in Boisar. In addition, a 
multiproduct facility coming up in Saudi Arabia for transmission line and solar products. 
 
As of the current quarter end, our aggregated installed capacity stood at 889,200 metric tons per 
annum, excluding rolling and galvanizing capacity, which are utilized for captive consumption. 
Let me briefly explain our product offerings. 
 
For our solar business, we manufacture structural components required to install and support 
solar panels. This includes structures for both fixed-tilt and tracker-based plants. Our product 
portfolio includes cold-rolled module mounting structures, tracker piles, torque tubes, couplers, 
purlins, and stamp parts. 
Since we manufacture components for both types of solar plants, customers can source most of 
their structural requirements from us. This is what allows us to offer customers a one-stop-shop 
solution for their solar structural requirements. 
 
Moving to wind energy. We manufacture both tubular and hybrid lattice towers used to support 
wind turbines. In the manufacturing line vertical, we provide infrastructure that enables 
electricity generation at source to reach its end customers. The lattice transmission towers are 
for lines up to 1,200 kV, along with transmission hardware such as insulator fittings, suspension 
clamps, and vibration dampers. 
 
Within  the fasteners, we have products such as bolts, nuts, studs, washers, and specialized 
industrial fasteners. These are used for solar, wind, transmission, bridges, and railways. So in 
simple terms, Karamtara provides the structural backbone and critical across the renewable 
energy and power transmission value chain. While its fasteners business provides additional 
exposure to several industrial sectors. 
 
During the past two years, we have expanded our installed capacity substantially by 
debottlenecking our existing facilities. We have commissioned new facilities in Boisar, 
Maharashtra, and at Bhachau, Gujarat. The new Bhachau cluster is strategically located near 
major renewable energy hubs such as Khavda, Rahpar, and Jamnagar, support supporting 
efficient access to key markets domestically. 
For international markets, the facility is connected to the close-by Mundra and Kandla port. As 
mentioned previously, we are also setting up one multiproduct facility coming up in Saudi

becoming an increasingly important pillar for India's renewable energy transition. India is 
already among the leading wind power markets globally and has substantially untapped wind 
potential. 
The industry is being supported by increasing tender activity, Renewable Purchase Obligations, 
and the government's long-term renewable energy objectives. The growth in renewable 
generation also makes transmission infrastructure critical to the energy transition. 
 
For Karamtara, these industry trends directly translate into business opportunity. Solar requires 
mounting structures and trackers. Wind requires towers, and renewable projects require 
transmission infrastructure. Our presence across all three segments allows us to participate 
across the broader energy transition opportunities. As India expands renewable capacity and 
strengthens its power grid, we see multiple structural growth drivers supporting Karamtara's 
long-term growth. 
 
In fact, currently, we are witnessing a market where demand continues to outpace supply, 
creating a favorable environment for us. Our large installed capacities give us flexibility to 
accept orders, which is the parameters that align with our strategic objectives while maintaining 
discipline on commercial terms.

accelerating renewable energy sector growth story while continuing to serve stable international 
markets, providing diversification and multiple avenues for sustainable growth. 
 
Our customer relationships remain at the center of our growth. Our broad product portfolio and 
are positioned us a one-stop partner for our customers, allowing us to serve multiple 
requirements and increase our share over time.

confidence to return to us with repeat orders. Our ability to retain and deepen these relationships 
is built on three key strengths: the quality of our products, the capacity we have built, and our 
ability to deliver.

contributing 82% of Q1 FY27 revenues. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR174 crores, 
reflecting a 45% growth on year-on-year basis.

performance on an annual basis rather than on solely on the quarterly basis. Talking about our 
annual performance, for FY27, we endeavor to grow our revenues by 60% to 65% over the last 
year.
